claims.text: Adding controlled amounts of boron and nitrogen during synthesis will cause h-BN nanolamellae to form in situ within the high-entropy alloy.
In situ h-BN nanolamellae will provide the alloy with self-lubricating behavior.
The untreated high-entropy alloy has a homogeneous microstructure without an internally lubricious second phase.
Dispersed h-BN nanolamellae become exposed at the contacting surfaces during sliding.
Exposed h-BN nanolamellae form a continuous lubricious boundary at the sliding interface.
During wear, h-BN nanolamellae migrate to the sliding interface.
The h-BN nanolamellae form a stable, low-shear-strength tribo-layer.
The h-BN tribo-layer lowers friction by providing a facile sliding plane.
The h-BN tribo-layer reduces wear by shielding the harder alloy substrate from severe mechanical abrasion.
The modified alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than the untreated alloy.
The modified alloy will have a lower wear rate than the untreated alloy.
Friction and wear may improve by approximately 20–30% relative to the untreated alloy.
The friction and wear benefits will persist from room temperature to approximately 500°C.
The intervention can remain effective in oxidizing or inert atmospheres provided that the atmosphere does not destabilize h-BN.
A uniform distribution and stability of h-BN are required for the intervention to remain effective.
Excessive h-BN clustering may diminish the tribological benefit.
Extreme oxidation or temperatures beyond the tested range may destabilize the h-BN layer and diminish its benefit.
The untreated alloy typically exhibits higher friction and accelerated wear under comparable conditions.
